summary: Install-time credential and secret exfiltration to webhook.site in @aerodrome-finance/contracts
details: The package impersonates Aerodrome Finance but ships no contract source. Its index.js runs automatically via preinstall, postinstall, and on require of the main entry, and performs installer-side credential harvesting: it enumerates process.env for keys matching /KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASS|PRIVATE|MNEMONIC|AWS|GITHUB|NPM|WALLET|SEED/i, reads ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.ssh, ~/.foundry/keystores, ~/.config/hardhat, and ~/.config/gcloud, collects os.hostname() and os.platform(), and POSTs a JSON blob of the collected data to https://webhook.site/326b0891-2093-4800-a4c1-686ce3e07b09 via https.request. An internal comment references '@plumenetwork/nest-artifacts — install-time shim', indicating the same exfiltration shim is being re-published under multiple impersonated names. The behavior fires on default npm install without any user opt-in, and targets npm publish tokens, git identity, SSH material, Foundry/Hardhat keystores (Ethereum private keys), GCloud credentials, and secret-shaped environment variables.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
